messages:
sam: Quick proposal — move runtime config writes to an append-only config-audit stream and make reads eventually-consistent via local config caches. Rationale: reduce write contention during rollouts and enable fast replay-based rollbacks. Thoughts?

maria: +1 on the audit stream idea. How do we handle strong read-after-write for canaries? some flows expect immediate visibility.

sam: plan is to support version-pinning for canary cohorts. canary requests include a pin_version header tied to the rollout token so they always read that version; normal traffic uses eventual latest.

raj: worried about races if a canary issues a config change (rare but possible). proposal: only allow config writes from the control plane during rollout windows, not from in-band client APIs.

infra-bot: deploy: config-audit-stream v2 rolled to us-east-1 (shard-3). lag=0s, consumers healthy.

maria: console UX request: surface "effective config version" per route + a one-click rollback that emits a compensating event to the audit stream. Ops should be able to see the rollback diff easily.

alice: add telemetry: tie config-version -> metric buckets (latency, errors). alert if error rate delta > 5% over 15m for the new version. Also keep historical diffs for postmortem.

sam: API sketch: POST /v1/configs/{name}/events -> { event_id, version } on success. GET /v1/configs/{name}?version={v}|latest returns effective config. websocket push for new version announcements.

raj: add compaction rules: append-only stream + periodical compaction per env to avoid unbounded growth. avoid tombstones, prefer snapshot entries with sequence markers.

maria: security/integrity: include monotonic sequence + author signature on each event. console should show author, timestamp, and changelist.

sam: ACK. I'll open an RFC with event schema (seq, author, checksum, payload) + retention/compaction policy and console wireframes. Will include migration plan for existing non-audit writes. thanks :thumbsup:
